About me

I’m a GN&C engineer at Nara Space in Seoul, South Korea. My work spans mission analysis and flight-algorithm development, alongside research on advanced AI and vision methods for space situational awareness (SSA) and rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO).

Previously I did my Ph.D. at the Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) in the Department of Aeronautics & Astronautics at Stanford University advised by Dr. Simone D'Amico. There, my research covered the complete pipeline of machine learning development for spaceborne computer vision applications, from dataset generation and neural network design to on-ground validation and integration into GN&C algorithms. Potential applications of my research include space situational awareness and logistics, such as active debris removal, inspection and refueling of defunct satellites.
